# Systems thinking
Systems thinking studies how feedback, delays, and structure shape behavior over time.

---

# Feedback loops
Feedback loops allow the consequences of an action to influence the next action in a system.

---

# Reinforcing feedback
Reinforcing feedback compounds change and can produce accelerating growth or decline.

---

# Balancing feedback
Balancing feedback counteracts deviation and pushes a system toward a target or constraint.

---

# Delayed effects
Delays between action and feedback make a system harder to understand and easier to overcorrect.

---

# Leverage points
A leverage point is a place where a small structural change can alter a system's behavior.

---

# Mental models
Mental models influence which signals people notice and which interventions they consider possible.

---

# Deliberate practice
Deliberate practice uses focused repetition and feedback to improve a specific skill.

---

# Fast feedback
Fast feedback helps a learner correct errors while the previous attempt is still easy to remember.

---

# Error signals
An error signal is useful when it is specific enough to change the learner's next attempt.

---

# Spaced practice
Spaced practice strengthens memory by revisiting material after some forgetting has occurred.

---

# Attention
Focused attention limits competing signals so that feedback can be interpreted more accurately.

---

# Small experiments
Small experiments reduce the cost of error while producing feedback about uncertain assumptions.

---

# Decision quality
Decision quality improves when feedback distinguishes signal from noise and updates assumptions.

---

# Learning metrics
Useful learning metrics measure changes in future performance rather than activity alone.
